title.narrative: USAID’s Education is The Response Activity (Elimu ni Jibu ya USAID)

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): DRC has significantly increased access to primary education. The net attendance rate increased from 52 percent in 2001 to 78 percent in 2018, though 7.6 million children aged 5-17 remain out of school. Adolescent girls in conflict settings are especially at risk of sexual and gender-based violence, which often leads to dropping out and further vulnerability. To address these challenges, FY 2022 funding for USAID's Education is the Response will increase children's access to education, create safer learning environments, and improve the quality of teaching and learning in schools. USAID/DRC focuses on girls, boys, and youth living in crisis- and conflict-affected and under-resourced communities...Equal access to quality education can create pathways for economic growth, improved health outcomes, sustained democratic governance, and more peaceful and resilient societies. Education is the Response builds the resilience of Congolese children and youth and provides grants to local organizations focused on child protection and education...USAID's Education is the Response advances the Integrated Country Strategy via Mission Objective 3.2 (Improve public institutions' responsiveness, respect for human rights and basic freedoms, and accountability, including through strengthening education overall) by strengthening community resilience, improving the quality of education services by non-state actors, and increasing the demand for and utilization of quality education......
